practice_description.practice_summary: Steyerl creates video essays, installations, and lecture-performances that interrogate the politics of images, data, AI, and digital circulation. She is one of the most influential voices on the political economy of visual culture in the age of machine learning.
practice_description.methodology: Steyerl works through essayistic film and lecture-performance, combining investigative journalism, critical theory, and visual experimentation. She frequently uses AI tools, 3D modeling, and data visualization as both subject and medium, exposing the power structures embedded in predictive technologies and image-making systems. Collaborates with teams of programmers, designers, and researchers at her UdK Berlin research center.

relevance_to_sense_room.relevance_summary: Steyerl's critical interrogation of AI prediction systems and data politics provides essential conceptual grounding for any art-first generative exhibition. Her work demonstrates how technological infrastructure is never neutral, making her a key reference for the Sense room's commitment to non-extractive, art-led intelligence.
relevance_to_sense_room.art_as_substrate: Partially. Her video essays and installations can function as substrate layers, but they are strongly authored works with specific critical arguments rather than open-ended generative material. Their power lies in framing and critique rather than composability.
relevance_to_sense_room.relational_composition: Her work is deeply relational in its analysis of image circulation, data economies, and networked power, but the artworks themselves are typically composed as singular authored statements rather than graph-based compositions.
relevance_to_sense_room.self_recomposing: Some installations (e.g., 'This is the Future', 'Power Plants') include generative or interactive elements that respond to data inputs, but the core video essays are fixed. Her lecture-performances are inherently live and responsive.

works.title: This is the Future
works.description: Immersive video installation at the Venice Biennale exploring AI prediction, featuring a garden of power plants generated by neural networks. The work asks what AI predicts and for whom.
works.relevance: Directly addresses AI prediction as political material. Demonstrates how generative imagery can be critically deployed in installation format.

works.title: Power Plants
works.description: Companion installation to 'This is the Future' where neural-network-generated flowers grow in response to environmental data, blending generative AI with botanical metaphor.
works.relevance: A generative, data-responsive installation that could serve as a model for graph-curated composition where art responds to relational inputs.

works.title: Duty Free Art
works.description: Book and lecture series examining art in the age of planetary civil war, freeports, and digital circulation. Argues art has become a financial instrument and data asset.
works.relevance: Provides the critical framework for understanding art's entanglement with data economies, essential context for any commons-oriented art infrastructure project.

protocol_art_resonance.protocol_art_summary: Steyerl's practice does not build protocols or infrastructure as artistic medium per se, but her critical analysis of existing systems (image circulation, AI training pipelines, prediction markets) constitutes a form of systems-level artistic inquiry that exposes protocol-level politics.
protocol_art_resonance.system_designed: No formal system or protocol. However, her UdK Berlin research centre functions as an informal infrastructure for critical AI-art research and pedagogy.

commons_orientation.commons_summary: Steyerl is a vocal critic of enclosure, extraction, and the commodification of art and data. Her writings advocate for commons-based alternatives, though her own work circulates through commercial galleries (Andrew Kreps, Esther Schipper) and major institutional exhibitions. She has written extensively on free circulation vs. exploitation of digital images.

governance_model.governance_detail: Steyerl is the primary author and decision-maker of her works, though she collaborates with technical teams and researchers. Her UdK research centre involves collective research processes, but the artistic output is primarily author-driven.

consent_and_authorship.consent_approach: Steyerl's work frequently interrogates questions of consent in data harvesting and AI training. Her own practice uses publicly available imagery and data, often critically reframing material to expose power asymmetries in image economies.
consent_and_authorship.authorship_model: Solo authorship with collaborative production. Steyerl is the named author; technical collaborators and researchers contribute to production but the conceptual authorship is singular.

liveness_and_duration.temporal_detail: Video essays are fixed-duration works, but installations like 'Power Plants' include generative elements that evolve in response to data. Lecture-performances are inherently live and unrepeatable. The overall body of work is continuously evolving in response to technological and political shifts.

data_materiality.data_sources: Found images, news media, surveillance footage, AI-generated imagery, neural network outputs, environmental data, art market data, publicly available datasets
data_materiality.data_provenance: Primarily uses publicly available and institutional sources. Her work critically examines data provenance itself as subject matter. No known ethical controversies regarding her data use.

embedding_space_relevance.embedding_summary: Steyerl engages with latent spaces and AI image generation as subject matter rather than artistic tool per se. Works like 'This is the Future' and 'Power Plants' use neural network image generation, engaging directly with the latent space of GANs. Her critical writing addresses how embedding spaces encode bias and power.

exhibition_modality.spatial_description: Large-scale immersive video installations typically occupying darkened gallery spaces with multiple screens, sculptural elements, and spatial audio. Lecture-performances transform institutional spaces into sites of critical pedagogy.

interoperability.composability: Low composability. Steyerl's works are strongly authored, self-contained critical statements. They do not expose APIs or produce outputs designed as inputs for other systems.
interoperability.technical_openness: Closed system. Works are exhibited through institutional and gallery frameworks. Critical writings are published but artistic works are not open-source or forkable.

technical_approach.stack: Video production and editing, 3D modeling and rendering, GAN-based image generation, custom neural network pipelines, Unity (for some installations), spatial audio systems, LED and projection hardware

network_position.scene_affiliation: Post-internet art, critical media art, Berlin art scene, institutional art world (Venice Biennale, documenta, Serpentine), critical AI/technology discourse, UdK Berlin academic community, e-flux publishing network
network_position.connections: K Allado-McDowell (shared territory of AI and creative practice), Yuk Hui (shared critical technology discourse, both engaged with non-Western technology perspectives), Trevor Paglen (surveillance and AI), James Bridle (New Aesthetic, AI critique)

potential_role_in_adai.role_detail: Steyerl's critical framework on AI, data politics, and image economies is essential intellectual infrastructure for A(DAI). Her work provides the critical language for understanding why commons-first, art-led approaches matter. She could serve as a conversation partner or advisory voice, though her institutional position and profile may make direct collaboration complex.
